newsitem.title: UK: Gas/electricity arbitrage set to boom in UK - BP.
newsitem.headline: Gas/electricity arbitrage set to boom in UK - BP.

text.p: The U.K. is set for a huge increase in the amount of electrical power generated by gas, with well over half of all electrical supply potentially coming from gas in the next few years, a conference was told on Tuesday.

Tony Fountain, director of trading, transportation and sales at BP Gas, said U.K. electrical demand now stands at 65 gigaWatts. Of this 15 gigaWatts was supplied by gas plants already commissioned, or soon will be by new plant under construction.
But Fountain said BP believes gas plant will eventually total 21 gigaWatts of electrical power when more projects come through.
"And if 21 gigaWatts is the BP figure, we can also identify a total of 40 gigaWatts of projects which in principle people would like to build," he said.

"If all these projects went ahead, there'd be enough gas use in power generation to double current U.K. demand. It shows that gas at current prices (assessed by Fountain at 14 to 15 pence a therm) is by far the most economic way of generating electricity," he added.

The reason for the surge of interest in gas generation was that "there are huge margins between gas at those levels and electricity", although Fountain warned that this was not a sustainable differential.

"The next trader BP employs will be an electricity trader, and the "spark arb", the arbitrage between gas and electricity, will be important, just as crack trading between crude and products is important in oil trading."

Fountain acknowledged that the growth in gas-powered generation could lead to a fall in electricity prices and so to lower margins between gas and electricity, just as oversupply has led to declining margins in oil refining.
"I don't know how it will develop, but develop it will", he added.
